title: Operadic colimit cocones exhibit relative free algebras
statement:
Use the universe and presentably monoidal conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads and their algebra functor categories of [lem-coef-operadic-algebra-presentability], and the monoidal cocartesian fibration of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category]. Coherent transformations, mapping spaces and cocones have the meanings of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $u:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ be an inert-preserving map of small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operads, an equivalence on the zero-fibers, both of which are spaces. Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal and let $X:\mathcal C\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ be an algebra. An arrow in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is active when its opposite preserves both endpoints. For a color $d\in\mathcal D_{[1]}$ put $K_d=\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{act}})_{/d}$, where the active subcategory has all objects and just the arrows over active base maps. Write $T_d:K_d\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ for $X$ after source projection.

Here is the meaning of an operadically colimiting active cocone $T:K\to\mathcal V^\otimes_{\mathrm{act}}$ with apex $v\in\mathcal V$. A finite tuple is an object in a fiber $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[r]}\simeq\mathcal V^r$, including the empty tuple. Concatenation $\oplus$ means concatenation of these tuples, with coherent structure induced by the Segal equivalences. For finite fixed tuples $L,R$ and $w\in\mathcal V$, restriction along the cocone must induce an equivalence from the space of active arrows $L\oplus v\oplus R\to w$ to the space of coherent active cocones $L\oplus T\oplus R\to w$. An active arrow from a tuple over $[r]$ to $w$ lies over the unique active map $[r]\to[1]$; a coherent active cocone is a coherent transformation with all components of this form. Empty $L$ and $R$ are allowed.

There exist a $\mathcal D$-algebra $F$ and a transformation of $\mathcal C$-algebras $\eta:X\to u^*F$ for which, at every color $d$, the cocone $T_d\to F(d)$ induced by $\eta$ and the action of $F$ is operadically colimiting in this sense. Moreover, for any $\mathcal D$-algebra $F$ and $\eta$ with this cocone property, composition with $\eta$ induces natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal D}(\mathcal V)}(F,B)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal C}(\mathcal V)}(X,u^*B)$ for every $\mathcal D$-algebra $B$.
